args.query: Tarred Gull Bram Sela Kelp Mother

properties.role: Tide-reader who rows boats out of Gullwick
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, never meets the party's eyes and keeps her gaze on the tide line. Terse, shrugs, goes back to mending her net. Gives the party the ride but sets a hard limit: never at night.
properties.wants: To row only by day; leaves the party to their own risk after dark.
properties.knows: Her grandmother said Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang. Hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced; spelling varies (Sela/Sella).

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.

changes.why: Where the table last saw her; she waits at pier four.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Forty years ago the Saltmere Mine flooded the same night the drowned bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Links the mine to the bell's origin, per Sela.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. In the morning the fog sits on the docks; pier four has an upturned skiff where Sela mends nets.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: New description of the docks.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. The entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smelling of church candle wax comes out. About thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: closed; flooded with warm water about thirty paces in

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: GM's own description of the mine and its flooded state.

properties.what_is_open: Wet hymn-book pages float in the flooded mine; one has "M. Brand" in pencil in the margin, which Teo says is his sister Mira's handwriting. Why were hymn pages in the mine, and did Mira come here?
properties.next_step: Teo reads the chapel as the source of the hymns and wants to go there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: New lead; the margin note is narrated, that it is Mira's hand is Teo's claim.

sources.quote: Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: The pages are in Saltmere Mine.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Teo ties the pages to his sister.

properties.what_changed: Teo found a hymn page at Saltmere Mine with "M. Brand" in the margin and believes it is Mira's handwriting, so she was there.

sources.quote: And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: First physical trace of Mira for the goal.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master Maren Vosk is in the cult and running the choir.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Player theory, kept as a thread only; no fact about Maren changes.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this.

changes.why: The theory is about Maren.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out: just the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water, like a congregation, and vanish when the bell stops.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: GM's descriptions of the chapel and what the party saw.

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local legend; the GM did not confirm it, so it is a rumor.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.
And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago.

changes.why: The bell rang again with louder humming; the GM put the clock at three of six.

properties.details_shown: A tavern by the docks. Fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New place where the party sleeps.

properties.played_as: Huge man with a red beard who laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Gruff and generous: serves stew unasked, teases the party as brave or stupid, speaks warmly of Maren.
properties.wants: Looks after the party; no stated aim beyond that.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He runs the Tarred Gull.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: The fact is about Maren.

change.name: Dive to the drowned chapel at low tide

properties.what_is_open: The party plans to find what lies in the drowned chapel, since Teo reads the hymns as coming from there.
properties.next_step: Sela rows them out at first light and they dive at low tide; Vessa buys rope and a second lantern.
properties.deadline: First light the next day, low tide, daytime only.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: The party's agreed plan for the next session.

sources.quote: Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide.

changes.why: Sela is the boatwoman for the plan.

sources.quote: We go down to the chapel.

changes.why: The chapel is the destination.
